title: Assessment and Settlement of Service-Level Credits (Insurer Program Agreements)
content:
For each target a quarterly scorecard misses under the Insurer Program Agreements, a credit of the tier's credit per missed target is assessed, one per missed target, until the quarter's credits reach the tier's quarterly cap; the credit that would pass the cap is reduced to it and none follows. A tier whose credit is zero assesses none. A credit is settled once, by offset against the insurer's next repair invoices or by payment, within the tier's settlement period in days of the scorecard, naming the credit settled. Credits never reduce what a vehicle owner pays.

## The amount of each credit

The quarter's credits are the total of the credits already assessed for that scorecard quarter. Each credit assessed for a missed target is the lower of the tier's credit per missed target and the tier's quarterly cap less the quarter's credits already assessed. Once the quarter's credits equal the cap, no further credit is assessed for that quarter.

Each credit is recorded as one entry per missed target per quarter, showing the assessment date, the quarter, the target missed (cycle time, customer satisfaction, reinspection pass or supplement frequency) and the amount as a positive figure. Credits assessed add to what the network owes the insurer; credits settled reduce it.

## Worked example (hypothetical tier figures)

Take a hypothetical credit of 400.00 per missed target and a quarterly cap of 1000.00, and a quarter whose scorecard misses all four targets.

| Missed target, in turn | Quarter's credits already assessed | Cap less credits already assessed | Credit assessed |
|---|---|---|---|
| First | 0.00 | 1000.00 | 400.00 |
| Second | 400.00 | 600.00 | 400.00 |
| Third | 800.00 | 200.00 | 200.00, reduced to the cap |
| Fourth | 1000.00 | 0.00 | None |

The quarter's credits come to 1000.00. With a hypothetical credit of 0.00 per missed target, no credit is assessed whatever the number of targets missed.

## Settlement

| Point | Rule |
|---|---|
| How often | Once per credit |
| How | Offset against the insurer's next repair invoices, or payment |
| By when | Within the tier's settlement period, in days of the scorecard |
| Reference | The settlement names the credit settled |

A settlement records its date, the credit it names, the method (invoice offset or payment) and the amount settled as a positive figure. Whether a credit has already been settled is read from the company's records of settlements naming that credit, before a settlement is recorded.

Hypothetical timing: for a scorecard published on 15 April with a 30-day settlement period, the credit is settled by 15 May.

## Basis questions

**Does a credit lower the vehicle owner's share of a repair?** No; credits never reduce what a vehicle owner pays.

**May a credit that has been settled be settled again?** No; a credit is settled once.
